weeks.label: Week 14 - Renal Anatomy, Filtration, Sodium, Water & Acid-Base

lectures.name: Anatomy of the Kidneys, Ureters, & Adrenal Glands

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• Filtration = Kf (ΔP − Δπ); obstruction ↑ Bowman's space pressure → ↓ GFR
  • RPF = (1 − Hct) × RBF; filtration fraction ~20% of RPF
  • GFR set by arteriole diameter: Ang II constricts efferent (holds GFR), prostaglandins dilate afferent
  • CHF + NSAID + ACEi → afferent constriction + efferent dilation → ↓↓ GFR
  • JGA: macula densa (TAL, senses tubular ionic content) + granular cells of afferent arteriole (store renin) + extraglomerular mesangial cells

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• RBF ~25% of CO; ~20% of RPF filtered
  • PCT reabsorbs 50–60% of solute + water; Na-coupled glucose/amino acids/phosphate
  • Fanconi = proximal RTA + glucosuria + phosphaturia + aminoaciduria; carbonic anhydrase inhibitors → NaHCO₃ loss
  • TAL: Na-K-2Cl (loop diuretics, Bartter); K⁺ back-leak → lumen + → paracellular Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺; loops → urinary Ca loss
  • DCT: Na-Cl (thiazides, Gitelman); major site of active Ca reabsorption; thiazides ↓ urinary Ca → Ca stones
  • CD: amiloride/triamterene block principal-cell Na channel; spironolactone = aldosterone antagonist (blood side)
  • Principal cell fails (↓ aldo, K-sparing) → ↑K⁺ + RTA; α-intercalated only → ↓K⁺ + RTA

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• House's law: ECF volume disorders = Na problems; serum [Na] disorders = water problems
  • RAAS fires in true ECF contraction (hemorrhage, diuretics) and "imagined" (CHF, cirrhosis, nephrotic)
  • Aldosterone → Na retention, K⁺ secretion, alkalosis; mimics: Conn's, Cushing's, licorice
  • ANP/BNP block CD Na channel → natriuresis; NSAIDs block PGs → Na retention, HTN, renal failure

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• ECF contraction: dry mucosa, ↓ turgor, tachycardia, flat JVP; postural tachycardia may be the only sign in the young → isotonic saline
  • ECF overload: edema, ascites, effusions, ↑ JVP; BP ↑ (renal) or normal/low (heart, liver) → diuretics/dialysis

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• ADH released mainly for ↑ osmolality; ECF contraction is weaker but ultimately potent
  • ADH → V2 → aquaporins in principal cells; also ↑ urea reabsorption in medullary CD
  • Non-osmotic ADH: ↓ effective volume, pain/stress, SSRIs, carbamazepine, CNS/lung tumours

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• Hypernatremia (Na >144) = water deficit; correct ≤10 mmol/L per day (cerebral edema); oral water or D5W
  • Hyponatremia (Na <136): check Posm; normal/high = pseudohyponatremia (glucose, mannitol)
  • Symptomatic → 3% saline first; asymptomatic → fluid restrict, ≤8–10 mmol/L/day
  • SIADH: 0.9% saline can lower Na further (hypotonic to a concentrated urine)

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• AG = Na − (Cl + HCO₃) ≈ 12; expected AG ↓ 3 per 10 g/L ↓ albumin
  • MUDPILES AGMA → check osmolal gap (2Na + urea + glucose); ↑ gap = toxic alcohol → fomepizole/ethanol ± HD
  • RTA: type 1 (α-intercalated) ↓K⁺; type 2 proximal HCO₃ loss; type 4 (aldosterone) ↑K⁺
  • Give HCO₃ when pH <7.10 (or HCO₃ <10–12)
  • Metabolic alkalosis = mineralocorticoid: primary (Conn's, HTN) vs secondary (vomiting, diuretics) → NaCl + replace K⁺

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• TTKG >7 = aldosterone working; <2 = absent/blocked or poor distal Na/flow
  • HyperK⁺: ECG first; Ca gluconate protects the heart; shift (insulin-glucose, β-agonist); then eliminate
  • Normal ECG → think pseudohyperkalemia (hemolysis, very high cell counts)
  • HypoK⁺: urine K >30 or TTKG >7 = renal wasting; oral preferred, IV <40 mmol/h

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• NS and RL → ECF only; colloid → plasma
  • D5W = free water: 2/3 ICF, 1/3 ECF; ½NS → 1/3 ICF, 2/3 ECF
  • 3% saline for symptomatic hyponatremia; D5W for hypernatremia

weeks.label: Week 15 - Renal Function, AKI & Chronic Kidney Disease

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• Creatinine clearance overestimates GFR (15–25% tubular secretion); inulin = gold standard
  • CKD-EPI underestimates GFR >60; cystatin C more accurate in children
  • BUN:Cr >80 = volume contracted (urea follows Na)

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• Dipstick detects ≥300 mg/day, misses immunoglobulins → UPEP for light chains
  • ACR: microalbuminuria 2–20 mg/mmol (dipstick negative); macro >20
  • Orthostatic proteinuria (adolescents) = benign
  • Nephrotic: >3.5 g/day, ↓ albumin, edema, lipids; MCD (children), membranous (Caucasian adults), FSGS (Black patients)
  • Child with nephrotic syndrome → prednisone without biopsy; adult → biopsy
  • Hematuria ≥3 RBC/HPF; glomerular = >70% dysmorphic RBCs, RBC casts, protein >1 g/day
  • RPGN (crescents) → high-dose steroids + IV cyclophosphamide/rituximab ± plasmapheresis

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• AKI: ↑ Cr 44 or >50% from baseline, or CrCl ↓ 50%
  • Sudden anuria → postrenal; renal U/S for hydronephrosis
  • Prerenal: hyaline casts, low urine Na/FENa, BUN:Cr >80; ATN: muddy brown granular casts
  • AIN: drug hypersensitivity, not dose-dependent, fever/eosinophilia/rash, sterile pyuria + WBC casts
  • Atheroemboli after catheterization: livedo, purple toes; Cr does not improve with IV fluids
  • Urgent dialysis: AEIOU (acidosis, hyperK⁺, ingestion, overload, uremia)

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• CKD = damage or eGFR <60 for ≥3 months, not on dialysis/transplant
  • GFR <25% of normal → declines even if insult removed
  • Slow progression: ACEi/ARB, BP, lipids, glycemia; avoid NSAIDs/aminoglycosides/contrast

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• Earliest DN = microalbuminuria (30–300 mg/day)
  • Targets: A1C ≤7%, BP <130/80, ACEi/ARB
  • ACEi/ARB → efferent dilation; SGLT2i → afferent constriction; both ↓ intraglomerular pressure

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• Transplant = best survival + QoL of RRT
  • MMF more effective than azathioprine; CNIs nephrotoxic
  • Acute cellular rejection → pulse steroids + switch cyclosporine → tacrolimus

weeks.label: Week 16 - Urinary Infection, Obstruction & Urologic Malignancy

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• Uncomplicated cystitis: no culture needed; nitrofurantoin 5 d, TMP/SMX 3 d, or fosfomycin 3 g once
  • Asymptomatic bacteriuria: treat in pregnancy (e.g., cephalexin 7 d); not in LTC patients without urinary symptoms
  • Men: culture, treat ≥7 d; complicated = immunosuppressed, uncontrolled DM, structural, fever/flank pain

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• Retention: urethral catheter first
  • Post-obstructive diuresis after relief of bilateral/bladder-outlet obstruction; usually mild, self-limiting

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• Medical: α-blocker, 5-ARI, combination, PDE5i
  • Surgery if retention, stones, recurrent UTI/hematuria, upper-tract damage, or failed meds; TURP = gold standard

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• TRUS-guided biopsy needed for diagnosis (palpable nodule or ↑ PSA); imaging alone not sensitive enough
  • Active surveillance for low-grade disease

lectures.name: Approach to Scrotal Pain and Masses
lectures.title: Approach to Scrotal Pain and Masses

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• Torsion: sudden, rock-hard testis, no Doppler flow → surgical emergency (6–8 h)
  • Epididymo-orchitis: gradual, tender epididymis, UTI signs/fever
  • Varicocele: left, bag of worms; right-sided → image the retroperitoneum
  • Spermatocele = "third testicle"; hydrocele transilluminates

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• Painless gross hematuria + smoking → urothelial cancer until proven otherwise
  • Work-up: urine microscopy ± cytology, CT (excretory phase), cystoscopy

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html: • Nephrotic syndrome in a child → MCD → steroids without biopsy

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• Appendage torsion = most common acute scrotum in children; blue-dot sign; conservative (NSAIDs)
  • UDT: most descend by 3–6 months; operate by 18 months; retractile testis stays down when brought down
  • Bilateral non-palpable testes in phenotypic male = emergency (CAH, salt wasting)
  • Circumcision for pathological phimosis, paraphimosis, recurrent balanitis
  • Enuresis: >5 y; secondary = dry ≥6 months then regressed

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• ≥8 mm: <10% pass; medical expulsive therapy = α-blocker (tamsulosin)
  • Fever + obstructing stone = urgent drainage (nephrostomy/stent) → sepsis risk
  • Low calcium intake predisposes; keep normal Ca intake; thiazide for hypercalciuria

blocks.title: Schulich Reviews
blocks.html:
• Urgent dialysis: seizures/coma/confusion, pericarditis, uncontrollable ↑K⁺/acidosis/overload
  • PD = home, cheaper; transplant = optimal RRT
